area.hero.lede: Boilers and radiators, furnaces, central air and ductless systems, for Lincoln Park greystones, two-flats, cottages, courtyard buildings and lakefront high-rises. Family-owned since 1952, with the owner, Rob, still on the calls.

area.who.copy: City & Suburban is run from 1225 N Cleaver St, just south-west of Lincoln Park across the river. Rob, the owner, still runs the calls and does the diagnosis on the jobs that need it.
area.reviews.1.quote: I’ve worked with City & Suburban Heating & Cooling since we lived in our condo in Lincoln Park, and now that we’ve moved to a single-family home, they continue to help us maintain our system. Rob has been especially helpful—always consistent, reliable, and easy to work with. It’s great having a company we can trust for both service and ongoing maintenance. Highly recommend!
area.reviews.2.quote: Our furnace had been making this annoying scratching/grating noise since last winter, and when it started doing it every time the heat kicked on a few weeks ago, we finally called C&S. Rob came by and said the motor was on its last leg - he said we could replace the motor or the whole furnace and gave us pricing for both.
area.reviews.3.quote: Highly recommend this service. Responsive, reliable, and reasonable pricing. Twice in the past few years, Rob has fixed our aging furnace but this frigid Friday night it kicked the bucket for good. Saturday morning the guys were at our house putting up a new one. Excellent customer service, punctuality, and clear explanations. C&S Heating look for solutions to fix vs selling you unnecessary spare parts.
area.reviews.4.quote: Hello. When I had a problem with my boiler I called the first name I saw in the book. Because I didn’t do much research on City and Suburban I was afraid of paying a high price for service. I was incorrect. Rob Koehler showed up on time and fixed my boiler for a reasonable charge. I now had heat. Victory!
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a greystone, a cottage and a tower
area.scope.1.why: Many greystones and courtyard buildings still heat with steam or hot-water boilers. A boiler repair is a different job from a furnace one.
area.scope.2.why: Radiator-heated buildings have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits or high-velocity systems.
area.scope.3.why: Boilers sit in low basements; condensers go in gangways or on garage roofs off the alley. Access sets the labour.
area.scope.4.why: In two-flats and condo conversions, one boiler can serve several units, so the association decides on repairs.
area.scope.5.why: Fan coils on a building loop, with management approval, a certificate of insurance and booked elevator time.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. A well-kept boiler can run for decades; where it has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Lincoln Park building
area.buildings.1.title: Two- or three-flat
area.buildings.1.body: A shared boiler and radiators, or a furnace per unit after conversion. Condensers in the gangway or on the garage.
area.buildings.2.title: Frame house
area.buildings.2.body: Small forced-air furnaces in low basements. Ductwork is tight; ductless is often the cleaner way to cool.
area.buildings.3.title: Vintage condo building
area.buildings.3.body: A central boiler with radiators in each unit. The association approves boiler work and any new cooling.
area.buildings.4.title: High-rise condo
area.buildings.4.body: In-unit fan coils on a building loop. Management approval and elevator booking first.

area.faq.heading: Lincoln Park HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Does my old boiler need replacing, or can it be repaired?
area.faq.1.a: Often it can be repaired. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: Can you add air conditioning to a radiator-heated greystone?
area.faq.3.q: Who decides on a shared boiler in a two-flat or condo?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a condo, mention who handles the shared boiler.
